annotations.title: Occasional leave in Poland: paid days off for a wedding, the birth of a child and a funeral (regulation on time off from work)

description: Use for paid days off for a wedding, the birth of a child or a funeral in Poland (urlop okolicznościowy): how many days for which relative (grandmother, grandfather, parents, siblings, in-laws) and the pay for those days. For maternity, parental and paternity leave, use plan_parental_leave. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Paid days off from work (urlop okolicznościowy) under § 15 of the Polish regulation on justifying absence from work and granting employees time off, with the rules in force now: 2 days for the employee's wedding, the birth of the employee's child, and the death and funeral of a spouse, child, father, mother, stepfather or stepmother; 1 day for the wedding of the employee's child and the death and funeral of a sister, brother, mother-in-law, father-in-law, grandmother, grandfather or a person supported by or under the direct care of the employee. Any other person (aunt, uncle, grandchild, brother-in-law) gives no day off. The employee keeps the pay (§ 16). With the gross monthly pay: pay per day and for all days off (gross pay divided by the working days of the current month). Always returns the table of all events. Only for employees with an employment contract, not for mandate contracts.

event.description: Event: the employee's wedding, birth of the employee's child, wedding of the employee's child, death and funeral. Default funeral.

gross.description: Gross monthly pay in PLN, for the pay of the days off.

relation.description: For funeral: who died. dependent = a person supported by or under the direct care of the employee; other = anyone else. Default other.
